skill.name: recurring-character-diary-comic
skill.description: Create, audit, and repair short page-native diary comics around an existing authorized recurring character, with story-directed page rhythm, exact dialogue, directional-surface proof, and original-resolution visual QA. Use when extending an established recurring-character series from an anecdote, conversation, dream, or viewpoint, or when checking or repairing identity, anatomy, text, prop, relation, continuity, or layout defects. Do not use for standalone character design, educational explainers, infographics, one-off illustrations, generic memes, unauthorized characters or marks, imitation of a named living artist, watermarking, or social-platform publishing.
skill.summary: A structured workflow for creating, auditing, and repairing page-native diary comics with recurring-character continuity.
skill.author: zseven-w

content.value_statement: Turn a real observation, conversation, dream, or viewpoint into a coherent short comic while preserving an authorized recurring character. This skill locks story beats, visual relationships, dialogue, and continuity, then guides generation and original-resolution review.
actual_capabilities: Creates 4-8 panel page-native diary comic plans from a concrete anecdote or viewpoint.
Builds recurring-character profiles with identity invariants, episode variables, and forbidden drift.
Compares three structurally different page skeletons before selecting a reading path.
Locks speakers, exact dialogue, props, directional relations, and cross-panel state changes.
Audits generated pages at original resolution and 25% across contract and editorial axes.
Supports deterministic lettering and controlled local repair through the included compositor workflow.
limitations: It requires an existing original, public-domain, or explicitly authorized recurring-character identity.
It does not generate or distribute artwork by itself without an available image-generation workflow.
Generated images still require human review for identity, anatomy, text, relations, and layout accuracy.
It does not grant rights to characters, marks, fonts, dialogue, references, or final outputs.

use_cases.title: Personal Storytelling
use_cases.description: Convert a small daily observation into a short comic with clear beats, exact dialogue, and a consistent recurring character.

use_cases.title: Series Continuity
use_cases.description: Audit a new episode against approved identity, props, relationships, and previous state records before release.

use_cases.title: Controlled Repair
use_cases.description: Diagnose a page defect and apply a bounded local edit or disclosed lettering fallback without losing page-wide evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Draft a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill in Create mode. Turn my anecdote into a five-panel diary comic using the attached authorized character. List the story beats, exact dialogue, and one selected page structure before generation.
prompt_templates.scenario: First comic from a simple personal story

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Protect Continuity
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the approved character profile and this new episode brief. Identify stable identity details, episode variables, critical props, speaker ownership, and forbidden drift. Then prepare a page-native prompt.
prompt_templates.scenario: Adding an episode to an existing series

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Audit a Render
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this rendered page against the attached story and visual contracts. Check identity, anatomy, relations, continuity, exact text, reading path, panel rhythm, and thumbnail silhouette. Report evidence and blockers without editing.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: Repair One Defect
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this page first. If one named defect can be isolated, propose a constrained local repair and define the allowed pixel region. If text alone fails, use the page-native-unlettered lettering route. Recheck the exact final hash.
prompt_templates.scenario: Repairing a continuity or lettering failure

output_examples.input: A five-panel story about a recurring character trying to carry a melting ice cream home.
output_examples.output: A page plan with five ordered beats: purchase, careful walk, visible melt, improvised rescue, and a final reaction. Each beat includes character state, prop relation, speaker, and protected dialogue.

output_examples.input: A generated page where the final speech bubble contains incorrect wording.
output_examples.output: An audit that isolates exact-text failure, preserves the accepted full-canvas art, and recommends deterministic lettering with a character-by-character comparison.

output_examples.input: A new episode whose reference sheet has an unauthorized signature mark.
output_examples.output: A blocked profile review explaining that the reference cannot authorize the mark. The workflow requests a valid standalone reference or disables the mark before generation.

best_practices: Confirm character, reference, font, text, and publication rights before generation.
Lock story facts, identity invariants, exact dialogue, and directional evidence before writing the final prompt.
Inspect the exact final artifact at original size and 25% on both contract-fidelity and editorial-layout axes.
anti_patterns: Do not invent a permanent recurring character when no authorized identity reference exists.
Do not default to equal card grids, independent panels, or cosmetic rotation when the story needs page-native rhythm.
Do not accept a generated file, successful tool call, or visual resemblance as proof that continuity and exact text passed.

faq.question: What kind of input does this skill need?
faq.answer: It needs an anecdote, conversation, dream, or viewpoint that can become a self-contained four-to-eight-panel story.

faq.question: Can I use any character reference?
faq.answer: Use only an original, public-domain, or explicitly authorized recurring character reference with rights covering the requested output.

faq.question: Does the skill create images directly?
faq.answer: It prepares prompts, contracts, layouts, audits, and repair steps. Image creation requires a compatible image-generation workflow.

faq.question: How does it protect character consistency?
faq.answer: It separates stable identity invariants from episode variables, records forbidden drift, and checks identity across the final page.

faq.question: When should I use deterministic lettering?
faq.answer: Use it when the page direction passes but model-rendered dialogue is not exact. Keep the full unlettered canvas intact.

faq.question: Can it repair an existing comic page?
faq.answer: Yes. Audit first, isolate one named defect when possible, make a bounded repair, and recheck the repaired region and complete final page.
